title: Claiming a container couples assignment to an in_progress transition
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03).

`jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` always attempts the transition to in_progress. For a strategic container (an epic whose children are still open) that transition is correctly blocked by incomplete dependencies, so the claim itself fails with exit 4 — even though "this lead now owns driving this epic" is exactly the state a lead wants to record at intake. The error message does suggest the workaround (`jit issue assign <id> <assignee>` — "assign without starting work"), which is how this session proceeded, but the workaround loses claim semantics (lease/claims.jsonl) and the failure aborts compound shell chains.

Proposal:
1. Add `jit issue claim --assign-only` (or make claim on a dependency-blocked container record the claim without the state transition, with a notice), so container stewardship is claimable without violating the lifecycle.
2. Alternatively/additionally: document the intended pattern for leads claiming containers, if assign-without-claim is the deliberate answer.

## Success Criteria
- [hard] REQ-01: a lead can record ownership of a dependency-blocked container in one command without a state transition and without a nonzero exit, via a claim variant or documented equivalent; covered by a CLI test claiming an epic with open children.
- [hard] REQ-02: the chosen mechanism is documented (command help + docs/) including how it interacts with leases and `jit claim` worktree semantics.

## Resolution

Delivered by the existing `jit issue claim --assign-only` flag: it records the assignee without transitioning the issue to in_progress, so a lead can record ownership of a dependency-blocked container in one command with a zero exit (REQ-01). The flag is documented in command help and `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` (REQ-02) and covered by `test_claim_assign_only_sets_assignee_without_transition` in `crates/jit/tests/exit_code_tests.rs`. Closed as resolved; no further implementation required.
